symbols.name: indeterminate
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of the one-dimensional ring, whose powers index positions.
symbols.quote: Let $x$ be an indeterminate, a formal symbol that is never evaluated, whose powers index positions.

symbols.name: axis indeterminate
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of axis i in the multidimensional target ring.
symbols.quote: where $x_i$ is the indeterminate of axis $i$.

symbols.name: axis exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent of x_i in a monomial of the target ring, an integer from 0 to lambda_i minus 1 for basis monomials.
symbols.quote: Its monomials $x_1^{\eta_1}\cdots x_D^{\eta_D}$ have $\eta_i$ as the exponent of $x_i$ (the letter $\eta_i$ changes meaning from earlier pages).

symbols.name: coefficient index
symbols.meaning: An ordinary coefficient index, an integer from 0 to Lambda minus 1.
symbols.quote: Let $e$ be an ordinary coefficient index, $0\le e<\Lambda$.

symbols.name: exponent
symbols.meaning: A nonnegative integer exponent of Phi(x) in the order argument.
symbols.quote:
For an integer $
u\ge 0$ (an exponent; the letter changes meaning from earlier pages), $\Phi(x)^
u=\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i
u}$ equals $1$ exactly when $\lambda_i\mid
u$ for every $i$, because each $\mu_i$ is invertible modulo $\lambda_i$.

symbols.name: axis coordinate
symbols.meaning: The coordinate of the index e on axis i, an integer in [0, lambda_i).
symbols.quote: Let $\gamma_i\in[0,\lambda_i)$ be the coordinate of $e$ on axis $i$, the exponent of $x_i$ in $\Phi(x^e)$ reduced modulo $\lambda_i$ (the letter $\gamma_i$ changes meaning from earlier pages).

relations.quote: It is applied to a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) of length $\Lambda$ and turns it into a multidimensional cyclic convolution whose axes have pairwise coprime lengths.

It is the step of the [exact multiplication algorithm](main-theorem.md) that places the coefficients of a [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) on distinct prime cyclic axes, so that later steps can transform each axis separately.
The Chinese-remainder map computes its coordinates from the [mixed-radix digits](mixed-radix-digits.md) of $e$.

relations.quote: Define $\Phi$ on the generator $x$ by $\Phi(x)=\prod_{i=1}^D x_i^{\mu_i}$; it is extended to polynomials as a [ring homomorphism](ring-homomorphism.md), which is well defined because $\Phi(x)^\Lambda=\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i\Lambda}$ and each $\lambda_i$ divides $\Lambda$, so every factor is $1$.
